chunks: Do they seek a judgement of the days of pagan ignorance? But who could be a better judge than God for those who are firm in their faith?

key_terms.الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: Pre-Islamic ignorance; a state of spiritual and moral ignorance before the advent of Islam
key_terms.يُوقِنُونَ: Those who are firm in faith or certain

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Hukm al-Jahiliyyah' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to critique the substitution of divine Sharia with man-made customs or tribal traditions, emphasizing that true certainty (Yaqeen) requires adherence to God's perfect judgment. It serves as a foundational argument for the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Imams as the interpreters of this divine law, distinguishing them from those who revert to Jahiliyyah in practice despite claiming faith.
